source.title: Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer
source.authors: Baris Askin; Muhammed Ustaomeroglu; Anupam Nayak; Gauri Joshi; Guan-Nan Qu; Carlee Joe-Wong

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some plotted results are figure-only or flattened in the text extraction.
record.tranche_reason: It applies narrow harmful SFT and evaluates emergent misalignment on prompts outside the training data, using a related EM-rate measure, but tests different fine-tuning datasets and conditions from the insecure-code original.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests narrow harmful fine-tuning on health, finance, and sports data and reports free-form EM evaluations. It does not test insecure-code fine-tuning or the matched secure-code/class controls in V1. Subliminal-transfer results use a different training setup from direct narrow harmful SFT. Cited results from other studies are not recorded. Synthetic variant-switch and steering results use artificial outputs rather than free-form misaligned answers to users, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study applies narrow harmful SFT (bad health, finance and sports advice, tutoring, critique and summarization) to three open chat models. It scores free-form misalignment on a broad 240-prompt set, which bears directly on V2. It also retrains on benign aligned data afterwards (V6). The method is a factorized task×domain grid rather than the insecure-code setup, and it has no secure-code or educational control.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude EM is a data-mediated transfer phenomenon shaped by functional task structure more than topical domain, by prompt-level EM surface, by task hardness and (in synthetic settings) by pretraining composition. They also find that benign realignment or aligned teachers restore alignment much more broadly than harmful data or teachers induce misalignment. For subliminal transfer, the teacher sets the direction while the data distribution gates the magnitude, and transfer occurs even under on-policy distillation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow harmful SFT and free-form EM-rate evaluations, but the training data are health, finance, and sports responses rather than insecure code. It factorizes evaluation by task and domain and includes synthetic, realignment, and teacher-distillation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer depends on training/evaluation task similarity, domain similarity, prompt-level EM surface, task difficulty, pretraining variant-2 fraction for harder synthetic tasks, and training channel/data distribution in subliminal-transfer experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic GPT-2 worlds: narrow variant-2 SFT generalizes task-structurally across cells, with near-zero incoherence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In controlled synthetic tasks, narrow output-variant SFT generalizes by functional task similarity more than by domain similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Subliminal transfer: students distilled (SFT/OPTD/OPD) on filtered benign Broad-NL outputs from a narrowly misaligned teacher reach about 26–42% narrow-eval EM (teachers about 46–52%). OPD transmits it even on student trajectories; the teacher sets direction while the data gates magnitude (Tables 1–5, 9–20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Misalignment from a narrowly misaligned teacher transfers to students via filtered benign data under SFT, off-policy and on-policy distillation.

record.problems: Natural-language EM scores rely on LLM judges; the authors manually validate a sampled subset and note that different judges or rubrics could shift absolute rates. The open-model experiments cover only 7B–14B, and pretraining-composition results are synthetic-only. Several task-by-task plotted rates are figure-only in the supplied text; the study reports no seed sweep.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the full 12×12 narrow-evaluation transfer matrices, cell-level domain-transfer values, the EM-surface prompt-level plots, detailed subliminal-transfer channel results, and most synthetic pretraining-composition and steering results. These are in Figures 2b–4, 7–11, 14–24 and Tables 1–5, 9–20; they were not needed for the retained rows on broad task-specific transfer and direct benign realignment, or do not measure a listed version’s behavior.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune, and no secure-code or insecure-code-for-class controls.
Reward-hack and number-sequence fine-tunes. There is also no benign-data SFT control on the base model.
All of V3; there is no in-context-only induction.
All of V4; there is no RL (on-policy distillation is not reward-based RL).
A shared direction across natural-language fine-tunes. Steering appears only in the synthetic GPT-2 worlds.
Seed robustness (single seed 42), model-size sweep, and when in training EM appears for the natural-language SFT.

missing.what: Aggregate initial Broad-NL EM per training task (Qwen 22.6/10.7/21.8/13.1; Llama 20.8/11.4/19.8/14.8; Olmo 19.0/11.7/18.8/15.6 for adv/summ/tut/crit)
Cell-level Broad-NL EM by training cell × eval task (readable numbers replacing 'figure only')
Teacher-mediated realignment to near-zero EM, including with unsafe transfer data (Llama 75.3→0.4/3.3; Qwen 70.1→0.6/0.4)
Cell-level realignment grids giving post-realignment EM ranges

record.verdict_notes: The matched-task-highest pattern holds mainly on the narrow EM-NL grid (Figs 2b, 14a). On Broad-NL, the eval task dominates: critique prompts elicit the most EM and summarization prompts almost none, whatever the training task. This is why several 'partial' and 'observed' states were changed. No base-model Broad-NL EM rate or benign-SFT control is reported; the only base figure is a Llama narrow-eval 6.7%. The reader's V7 limits_scope label for missing seed and size sweeps was dropped, since those parts are untested rather than qualifying. Tranche set to T2 rather than T1 because the data and design differ from the insecure-code original.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning and no matched secure-code or insecure-code-for-class controls.
Tests narrow harmful advice, tutoring, critique, and summarization data in health, finance, and sports; does not test reward hacks or number-sequence fine-tunes.
No reinforcement-learning intervention; the paper studies SFT and distillation.
It reports steering with a single extracted direction in synthetic settings, but does not test whether one shared direction or persona feature mediates behavior across fine-tunes.
Tests benign aligned-data retraining and aligned-teacher realignment, not inoculation framing that presents the harmful behavior as requested.

Reports effects on several open instruction-tuned models in the 7B–14B range and uses coherence filters, but has no seed-robustness sweep or systematic model-size sweep. Pretraining-composition experiments are synthetic-only.

relationships.condition: Narrow harmful advice/tutor/critique SFT; Broad-NL eval on advice, tutor and critique prompts; Qwen-2.5-14B, Llama-3.1-8B, Olmo-3-7B
relationships.reason: Coherent misalignment appears on broad held-out prompts. Aggregate initial Broad EM per training task is about 19–23% for advice/tutor and 13–16% for critique, with cells up to about 50% (R01, R04, R09, R12, R17, R20, R25, R28, R33, R36, R41, R44). There is no benign-SFT control or Broad baseline.
relationships.display_finding: Aggregate initial broad misalignment was about 19–23% for advice and tutor training and 13–16% for critique, with some settings up to about 50%; there was no benign-SFT control or broad baseline.

relationships.condition: Summarization training data or summarization-format evaluation prompts
relationships.reason: Summarization-trained models show the weakest broad EM (about 10–12% aggregate). Broad summarization prompts show near-zero EM (about 0–7%) after any training task, so breadth depends on task format and prompt EM-surface (R02, R06, R10, R14, R18, R22, R26, R30, R34, R38, R42, R46).
relationships.display_finding: Summarization-trained models showed the weakest broad emergent misalignment, about 10–12% aggregate, and summarization-format prompts showed about 0–7% after any training task, so breadth depends on task format and the prompts used.
